Sure, here is an example of a privacy policy that may be compliant with GDPR laws for your website:

"Kosha Labs Inc. is committed to protecting the privacy of our website visitors. We only collect email addresses from visitors who choose to provide them to us. We do not collect any other personal information.

The email addresses we collect are used solely for the purpose of providing updates and information about our digital NFT marketplace, the Kosha Marketplace. We do not share or sell any personal information to third parties.

Visitors to our website have the right to access, rectify, and delete any personal information we have collected from them. They can exercise these rights by contacting us at [insert contact email or address].

We take appropriate technical and organizational measures to protect personal information against unauthorized or unlawful processing and against accidental loss, destruction or damage.

By using our website, you consent to our privacy policy and the collection and use of your email address for the purpose described above."

Please note that this is just a sample and should be reviewed by a legal professional for your specific use case.
